images.prompt:
Korean webtoon panel, digitally inked and coloured by a professional webtoon studio. Crisp black ink with tapered strokes, heavier on the outer silhouette, the jaw, the hair mass and where forms overlap. Flat local colour with one hard-edged cool cel shadow per material. One named key light: its colour washes smoothly over the lit side. If the scene names a back light, it draws a thin crisp rim along the figure's silhouette. Everything else stays flat. Muted cool base palette of slate, navy and grey-blue, so the light source and the character's signature colour carry the saturation. Background simplified and lower in contrast than the characters. Small crisp highlights; glossy specular only on metal and wet surfaces.

Hand-made webtoon colouring: each garment has only a few large, opaque, clean-edged shadow shapes, placed in its real folds; no scattered translucent streaks, zigzag shards or crumpled-foil folds. Worn cloth shows a few small frayed notches and loose threads, never sawtooth edges along every edge. Plain shoes and clothes with no logos, stripes or brand marks. Every strap, buckle, pocket and seam is attached and has a purpose; no stray stitch marks. Matte skin, hair and stone; no 3D, low-poly or plastic look.

Recipe: establish. Single landscape production location key exactly 1536x1024 PNG. Camera is HIGH, 12 m above the water near the entrance side, tilted down enough to see the round floor and the back wall, wide lens without fisheye distortion. Named key light: dim pale daylight from a small pale-glazed circular oculus at the top of the dome and a few narrow pale-glazed clerestory slits. Show these actual light openings. Cool slate, dark blue water, cool grey-violet cel shadows, dull bronze accents. Room dim but every architectural route readable. Upper calm zone is the dome.
Use case: illustration-story. Asset boss_chamber_bells/key.png, INTACT state before chapter 17's destructive toll. A ROUND domed Far Side stone chamber, 30 m diameter, 25 m high to the crown. The floor is a clear circular pool of knee-deep dark water, 0.5 m deep; it is not a long basilica. Twelve massive ash-grey limestone pillars are arranged along the circular perimeter and support large arches below a ribbed stone dome; pillars do not fill the centre. Many silent green-patinated bronze bells of differing sizes hang mouth-down from sturdy iron chains connected to the dome ribs, largest bells about 3 m, never heads or monsters. All bells immobile. Keep a broad empty combat area in the middle. No bell-ringer boss or other creature.
Critical fixed geography: viewed from the FRONT entrance toward the BACK wall. The front bronze double doors are behind the camera, NOT in the back wall. At the exact middle of the BACK wall is a SMALL dark pointed doorway, approximately 2.2 m tall and 1.2 m wide; its SILL is precisely 6 m above the submerged chamber floor, only about 5.5 m above water. It is not a giant portal. A narrow unbroken stone wall stair starts low at the LEFT side of the back wall, curves upwards along the circular wall, and ends at a tiny stone landing at that high doorway. About 33 ordinary 18 cm risers make the elevation. No rail needed, but all steps are connected to solid stone. There is no second stair, no rear bronze double door. The dome is intact, all major ribs continuous, no collapse or rubble piles. Ancient wear and a few hairline mortar cracks only.
Exactly two very tiny generic adults, 1.75 m tall, in plain charcoal expedition clothing without logos, wading close to the bottom of the back stair for scale. One tests the bottom step with a staff; the other faces the high doorway, one hand on the wall. Both have adult 7.5-head proportions, long legs submerged to knees, feet grounded on the submerged floor. High camera sees head tops, correct common floor plane and perspective. Doorway sill is about three-and-a-half adult heights above the FLOOR, room crown fourteen adult heights. All dimensional relationships readable. No named cast, no glyphs.
The two input images are APPROVED V2 rendering references ONLY, for hand ink, matte old stone and dark wet reflections, not their rectangular room layouts. Do not copy green sky, industrial anchor chains, floor plates, modern lamps, pipes or cars. A round bell room with a dome and a humble high escape doorway, as specified. No collage or inset.
